runs.title: Microsoft's 'Code Red' outage: what actually happened?
runs.prompt: Microsoft declared a 'Code Red' alert to staff after what is being called a historic 24-hour outage of its M365/cloud services around November 20-24 2026. Find out, from public pages, (1) what services went down and how many users were affected, (2) roughly how long the outage lasted, and (3) what Microsoft or its executives have said about the cause and their response. The Reuters exclusive is the key source, but note many news sites paywall it. Start at https://www.reuters.com/business/microsoft-declares-code-red-after-historic-outage-internal-memos-show-2026-11-24/ and https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/microsofts-historic-cloud-outage-exposed-an-engineering-fog-of-war/ and https://www.foxnews.com/us/microsoft-declares-code-red-historic-service-outage
runs.answer: Per Wikipedia's article on the event (citing BBC, Guardian, Forbes, The Register), the outage hit Outlook, Teams, Exchange Online and Copilot — plus search surfaces like Bing, DuckDuckGo and even ChatGPT search — starting around 17:54 UTC on Nov 12, 2026, with Microsoft acknowledging Exchange Online mailbox failures, broader global problems by 18:07 UTC, and partial recovery from 04:36 UTC Nov 13; BBC described "almost 24 hours of disruption" and service was restored by Nov 14. Scale: roughly 430 million people use Microsoft 365 worldwide and issues were reported in more than 70 countries (Fox's headline calls it a 24-hour outage that "hit most of its users"), with governments, hospitals, courts and airlines affected in the US, UK, Australia, Japan, the Philippines, Singapore, South Africa and Brazil. On cause and response, Wikipedia's infobox attributes it to "faulty server updates" (descriptions of the failure point to a small number of compounding problems, not an attack), and Microsoft publicly said it was "deeply sorry" for the disruption; the internal "Code Red" memo language comes only from the Reuters exclusive, whose headline is visible but whose text I could not read. runs.title: South Korea air-raid alert: what happened?
runs.prompt: On November 24 2026 South Korea issued a 'take shelter' warning to residents of an island after Russian military aircraft flew near its airspace, reportedly scrambling fighter jets. Find out from a public news source: exactly what type and how many aircraft were involved, where they were detected, and whether South Korea's government or military has said anything officially since. Keep it factual. Start at https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/24/south-korea-tells-island-residents-to-take-shelter-after-russian-military-aircraft-approach and https://www.stripes.com/theaters/asia_pacific/2026-11-24/south-korea-russia-scramble-aircraft-ulleung-23560956.html and https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2026/11/24/korea-Russia-warplanes-KADIZ-Ulleung-Island-emergency-alert/5211795507595/
runs.answer: South Korea's military never published an exact type or count: the Joint Chiefs of Staff said only that "several"/about five Russian military aircraft entered the KADIZ over the East Sea (Sea of Japan) early on Nov 24, 2026 and approached the edge of South Korean territorial airspace near Ulleung Island (Ulleungdo) before leaving, with no airspace violation — which triggered the island's emergency shelter alert and the scrambling of South Korean F-15Ks. Russia's own Defense Ministry identified the aircraft as two Tu-160 Blackjack strategic bombers escorted by Su-35S and Su-30SM fighters (The War Zone), a figure Seoul has not confirmed. Officially, the JCS issued a statement the same day, the Ministry of National Defense summoned Russian defense attaché Col. Nikolai Marchenko at Yongsan to lodge a stern protest (he said "no comment"), and the foreign ministry conveyed regret to Russia through diplomatic channels. I found no public government or military statement dated after Nov 24 in the coverage available, and roughly 20-minute KADIZ transit times were reported.

runs.answer: A federal grand jury in Los Angeles (C.D. Cal.) returned an indictment on Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026, charging Thomas Markle, 81, with two counts of knowingly possessing child sexual abuse material — specifically 35mm film negatives depicting children — on two dates, Oct. 30 and Nov. 4, 2026. The U.S. Attorney's Office said the negatives were of children under 12, and the indictment alleges he appears in at least two of the photos with a nude prepubescent girl; each count carries up to 20 years, so up to 40 years total. Status: he is in custody at the Pinellas County Jail in Clearwater, Florida, after a judge revoked his release on Nov. 10 (he had cut off his ankle monitor), and a judge has found him mentally competent to stand trial. He is expected to be transferred to Los Angeles for arraignment "in the coming weeks" — no specific arraignment date had been set in the reporting I could read.

runs.title: Pick the clearest Microsoft outage source
runs.prompt: You need a complete, readable (non-paywalled) account of Microsoft's 'Code Red' 24-hour outage of November 2026: what went down, how long it lasted, and what Microsoft said. Visit each candidate and report which single page is the most complete and accessible. Candidates: https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/microsofts-historic-cloud-outage-exposed-an-engineering-fog-of-war/ , https://www.foxnews.com/us/microsoft-declares-code-red-historic-service-outage , https://www.ctvnews.ca/sci-tech/article/microsoft-declares-code-red-after-historic-outage-internal-memos-show-reuters-exclusive/ , https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-microsoft-code-red-outage/
runs.answer: Pick The Globe and Mail (https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-microsoft-code-red-outage/): it renders the full Reuters story with every key detail, despite a subscription promo banner. The Nov. 12–13, 2026 outage lasted 24 hours and took down Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services worldwide, hitting governments from Australia and Japan to the US, trading firms and airline communications; Microsoft blamed an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July and said it was not cyber activity or AI. Microsoft declared a "Code Red" — its most severe internal alert — with M365 Core President Jason Henderson calling it the most customer-impacting incident in Exchange Online history, VP Amanda Silver describing a "fog of war" with 11,000+ messages across 11 Teams chats, a one-hour worldwide resolution target, and CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologizing. Ars Technica is a solid but shorter summary; Fox News returned only navigation chrome with no article text, and CTV's page was buried in nav/related-link clutter.
obstacles: Fox News page returned no article body (only nav/footer chrome)
CTV page text was dominated by navigation and related-headline lists, article body not reachable in the extract
Globe and Mail shows a subscription promo banner, though the full article text still rendered
